why.title: A website is a business decision. We treat it like one.

items.title: One small team, start to finish

principles: Show work early. You see progress every week, not at the end.
Keep the stack boring. Proven tools beat clever ones.
Write for visitors first, search engines second.

process.title: Five steps, no surprises.
process.intro: Every project follows the same path, with a dated schedule and a checkpoint at the end of each stage. Typical timings for a marketing site are shown below.

steps.title: Discovery
steps.body: We learn your customers, goals and constraints, audit what exists, and agree on scope, sitemap and success measures.

steps.title: Design
steps.body: Wireframes first, then full-fidelity designs for key pages on mobile and desktop. Two feedback rounds are built in.

steps.title: Development
steps.body: We build on a staging site you can open at any time, wire up content, forms and integrations, and tune performance.

steps.title: Testing
steps.body: Real-device checks, accessibility review, browser coverage, analytics and redirect verification before anything goes live.

steps.title: Launch
steps.body: A scheduled go-live, a monitored first week, training for your team and 30 days of included post-launch fixes.

faq.title: Questions, answered plainly.
faq.intro: Still wondering about something? Ask us directly.

items.q: How much does a website cost?
items.a: Every project is quoted at a fixed price after a short discovery call. Cost depends mainly on the number of unique page designs, custom functionality (such as a store or booking) and how much content we need to migrate. You get a written quote with exactly what is included before you commit.

items.q: How long does a project take?
items.a: A typical marketing site takes 5 to 8 weeks from kickoff to launch. Stores and sites with custom functionality usually take 8 to 14. The biggest factor is how quickly feedback and content reach us, and we will give you a dated schedule in the proposal.

Two structured feedback rounds in design and one in development are included. Rounds are consolidated so everyone gives feedback at once, which keeps projects on schedule. Work beyond that scope is quoted before we start it.

items.q: What do you need from us?
items.a: One decision-maker, timely feedback, and your content: copy, photos and product data. If you do not have copy yet, we can write it or work with your writer as an add-on.

items.q: Who owns the website when it is finished?
items.a: You do. At launch you receive the source code, design files and admin access. We never hold your domain or hosting hostage.

items.q: Do you offer support after launch?
items.a: Every project includes 30 days of fixes. After that you can choose a monthly care plan covering updates, backups, monitoring and a set number of changes, or you can manage the site yourself.

items.q: How do we communicate during the project?
items.a: You get a shared project channel, a weekly progress update with a link to the latest build, and a call at each milestone. We work in your time zone where we can.
